diagnostic_evidence.quote:
we actually do not need to fix how the remaining $b-1$ elements are chosen 
 as long as the first one is chosen according to line \ref{line:eq:batchfirst}

issues.failure_explanation: For a non-first element of a batch, the algorithm only maximizes the stale surrogate r_{under n} after deleting previously chosen elements; it is not chosen by a weak-greedy condition relative to the enlarged space V_n. The displayed chain uses sigma_{tilde n}(f_n) >= sigma_{tilde n+1}(f_{tilde n+1}), which compares different functions and different spaces and is not implied by monotonicity. In l^2 take F={e_1,-e_1,e_2} and b=2. An admissible tie choice is f_0=e_1 and f_1=-e_1; with the indexing used in the analysis, V_2=span{f_0,f_1}=span{e_1}, so |a_{1,1}|=dist(-e_1,V_1)=0 while sigma_{1+b-1}=sigma_2=1 because e_2 is still at distance 1 from V_2. This violates (P1); adding small old-direction components gives variants in which every non-first batch element is redundant while a far direction remains.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose or prove a quantitative independence/angle condition for every selected batch element, equivalently change the remaining-batch selection so that each f_n has a weak-greedy-type lower bound against span(V_{under n}, f_{under n},...,f_{n-1}), and then rederive the rates. Merely adjusting constants or the b-1 index shift cannot repair redundant or antipodal batch choices.
issues.overall_effect: The basic matrix estimate driving the batch analysis is not valid for Algorithm alg:wbg as stated. Consequently the Hilbert-space comparison with Kolmogorov widths, the polynomial and exponential rate statements, the stated asymptotic (2/3)^alpha loss, and the Banach-space analogues are all unreliable for b>=2; the numerical discussion that invokes the theoretical upper rate inherits this gap.
issues.title: Batch diagonal lower bound (P1) is false for the stated stale batch selection
issues.why_classification: The failing estimate is the root of all proved convergence-rate guarantees for the stated parallel stale-selection batch algorithm. The counterexample falsifies the lemma already for b=2, and similar admissible choices can make a batch add far fewer than b new directions. Preserving the claims requires changing the selection rule or adding a substantial hypothesis, or withdrawing the general rate guarantee; no local constant or indexing fix suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: Write B=ceil(2+(b-1)/4) and p=alpha-beta-1/2>0. The small-index case covers all M<4B, so to contradict sigma_M<=1 one needs C_1 M^{-p}>=1 up to M=4B-1, hence C_1>=(4B-1)^p. The stated second part of C_1 is only 4(B-1)^p. Already for b=1, B=2, alpha=2 and beta=1/4 (allowed, since beta<1/2), p=5/4; if the maximum is attained by this second term, C_1=4 but 4*7^{-5/4}<1, so the printed final inequality >=1 does not follow and the case is not covered.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Enlarge the second term of C_1(n,b) to at least (4 ceil(2+(b-1)/4)-1)^{alpha-beta-1/2} (for example (4 ceil(2+(b-1)/4))^{alpha-beta-1/2}), or prove the finitely many small-index bounds directly from part (i).
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the defective batch diagonal bound, part (ii) of the Banach-space rate theorem has an unproved small-index regime. The deficiency concerns only the constant in C_1(n,b); the stated exponent n^{-alpha+1/2+beta} and the hypotheses alpha>1/2, 0<beta<min{alpha-1/2,1/2} are not changed by the needed correction.
issues.title: Banach polynomial-rate small-index contradiction uses an insufficient constant
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant/case-split repair: it preserves the rate exponent, the parameter regime, and the advertised scope, and requires no new global proof architecture. It is separate from the batch (P1) failure because it would remain in the proof of the small-M case after that root was repaired.
